summary: The legal input ends at n = 1000, so every candidate square has at most seven decimal digits. That complete domain is too narrow for runtime scaling to distinguish exhaustive partition backtracking honestly; the implementation instead bounds every candidate and every possible cut pattern.

workload_bound.source_constraint: n is between one and 1000, so i squared is at most 1,000,000 and has at most seven decimal digits.

replacement_checks.evidence: For each of at most n candidates, a d-digit square has only 2^(d-1) placements of cuts between adjacent digits. The suffix recursion visits no more than the corresponding O(d 2^d) bounded search work, with d at most seven.

Cases cover the minimum input, a range before the next qualifier, two- and three-piece partitions, zero-valued pieces, qualifying endpoints, a three-digit bound, and n = 1000 over the complete legal domain.
